text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **
German composer JOHANN SEBASTIAN BACH was born on this day in 1685.
Australian journalist ALICE HENRY, who was also a lecturer on socialism and voting for women, was born in 1857.
Australian cartoonist JAMES CASE was born in 1884.
Australian author FRANK HARDY was born in Victoria in 1917. He left school at the age of 13 to become a labourer, and wrote "Power Without Glory" in 1950.
Australian diplomat ALAN RENOUF was born in 1919.
Member of 'The Seekers', KEITH POTGER, was born in Colombo in 1941 and migrated to Australia in 1948 to study medicine.
British actor TIMOTHY DALTON was born in 1944.
US keyboard player with 'Sly and The Family Stone', ROSE STONE, was born in 1945.
'Mungo Jerry' singer/ songwriter RAY DORSET was born in 1946. Their biggest hits were "In The Summertime" (1970), "Baby Jump" (1971), "Lady Rose" (1971) and "Alright, Alright, Alright" (1973).

UK singer/guitarist/ bass player and songwriter with 'Supertramp' ROGER HODGSON was born in 1950. Hits included "Dreamer" (1975), "The Logical Song" (1979), "Breakfast In America" (1979), "Take The Long Way Home" (1979) and "It's Raining Again" (1982).
** EVENTS **
1556 : England's first Protestant Archbishop of
Canterbury, THOMAS CRANMER, was burnt at the stake as a heretic.
1871 : OTTO von BISMARCK opened the first Reichstag or
Parliament in the newly created German Reich.
1884 : Unions were legalised in France for the first
time.
1896 : Britain's first cinema opened in London's
Piccadilly Circus.
1908 : French aviator HENRI FARMAN flew over Paris with
the first air passenger.
1918 : The Second Battle of the Somme, the last German
offensive in World War One, began.
1927 : The Nationalist Chinese forces of CHIANG KAI-SHEK
took the city of Shanghai.
1932 : Captain de GROOT, who stole the thunder from New

South Wales Premier LANG, by slashing the official ribbon at the opening of the Sydney Harbour Bridge, was taken to a mental hospital and discharged. He was then charged with having maliciously injured a ribbon valued at two pounds. De GROOT was fined five pounds, with four pounds expenses, for offensive behaviour at the opening.
1945 : British warplanes destroyed Gestapo headquarters
in Copenhagen, killing over 70 Nazis. The raid also killed civilians, including 86 schoolchildren, in Denmark's worst civilian disaster of the war.
1950 : A United Kingdom survey found only 46 percent of
British households had a bathroom.
1956 : FANNY DURACK, who won gold for Australia in the
100-metres freestyle at the 1912 Olympics in Stockholm, died at the age of 61. Her time was 79.8 seconds.
1960 : South African Police shot dead 56 people and
wounded another 162 at Sharpville, a black township near Johannesburg. About 15,000 people had been peacefully protesting against laws, requiring them to carry travel documents at all times.
1963 : The notorious ALCATRAZ PRISON in the bay of San
Francisco was closed.
1973 : New Zealand chief censor banned the Australian
film "The Adventures of Barry McKenzie".
1976 : DAVID BOWIE and IGGY POP were arrested in a hotel
room in Massachusetts, and charged with possession of marijuana.
1977 : Indian Prime Minister INDIRA GANDHI resigned.
1985 : On the 25th anniversary of the Sharpeville
massacre, riot police shot dead 17 blacks at Langa township in South Africa.
1988 : Queenland golfer IAN BAKER-FINCH won the
Australian Masters golf title.
1994 : The last Italian soldiers ended their 15-month
peacekeeping mission in Somalia.
1996 : GORAN PERSSON, a former finance minister, became
Swedish prime minister.
